notes.title: Neurodyne: Neural Pitch Manipulation with Representation Learning and Cycle-Consistency GAN
notes.bp: Pitch manipulation should change intonation or musical key without destroying the underlying voice and content.
notes.wh: Pitch, source, and filter cues are entangled, and paired in-tune/out-of-tune examples are scarce.
notes.naive: Use a DSP pitch shifter or a source-filter disentanglement model trained only on paired examples.
notes.ap: Learn a pitch-independent latent representation adversarially and use cycle consistency to create the missing pairing implicitly.
notes.mech: Neurodyne encodes speech while an adversary discourages pitch information in the latent; cycle-consistency trains conversion in both directions.
notes.math: The representation must preserve identity/content while making pitch a controllable variable, and cycle consistency supplies a constraint when aligned pairs are absent.
notes.eval: The representation must preserve identity/content while making pitch a controllable variable, and cycle consistency supplies a constraint when aligned pairs are absent.
notes.ww: The paper reports improved global-key and template-based pitch manipulation over its compared methods.
notes.limits: Music data, pitch range, cycle assumptions, perceptual protocol, and content preservation bound transfer to conversational voice conversion.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Theoretical proposal for a unified Bayesian model of adaptation in non-interactive and interactive speech production
notes.bp: A speaker changes production when hearing altered feedback or interacting with another person, and one model should explain both adaptations.
notes.wh: Non-interactive feedback and interactive accommodation are often modeled separately even though both change the speaker-listener system.
notes.naive: Use unrelated models for altered-feedback production and conversational accommodation.
notes.ap: Extend a unified Bayesian perception-production framework so adaptation is an inference problem over intended and heard speech.
notes.mech: COSMO-style latent variables connect production and perception; Bayesian updating changes beliefs about the speech system under feedback or interaction.
notes.math: Adaptation is posterior inference under uncertain sensory evidence, not merely a speaker-specific parameter fine-tune.
notes.eval: Adaptation is posterior inference under uncertain sensory evidence, not merely a speaker-specific parameter fine-tune.
notes.ww: The proposal shows how both experimental paradigms can be described within one Bayesian framework.
notes.limits: This is a theoretical proposal, not an independent behavioral validation; parameterization, priors, and task fit remain open.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: A Study on Speech Assessment with Visual Cues
notes.bp: Speech quality should be estimated when no clean reference exists, using visual context that may help explain what is audible.
notes.wh: Audio-only proxies can miss visible articulatory or scene evidence, while PESQ/STOI are imperfect targets rather than human usefulness itself.
notes.naive: Predict a quality score from a single audio stream and treat the proxy metric as intelligibility.
notes.ap: Fuse STFT audio features with visual embeddings in a dual-branch CNN-BLSTM attention model and jointly predict PESQ and STOI.
notes.mech: The model aligns spectral and visual information before multi-task regression; LCC compares predicted and reference proxy scores under noise.
notes.math: Multimodal evidence can improve prediction of a proxy while still inheriting the proxy’s limitations and the visual/audio distribution.
notes.eval: Multimodal evidence can improve prediction of a proxy while still inheriting the proxy’s limitations and the visual/audio distribution.
notes.ww: On LRS3-TED with DEMAND noise, the paper reports higher LCC than audio-only baselines for PESQ and STOI under seen noise.
notes.limits: Seen-noise conditions, proxy targets, visual availability, dataset, and correlation metric limit transfer; proxy prediction is not a listener study.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: MOVER: Combining Multiple Meeting Recognition Systems
notes.bp: A meeting recognizer should combine systems that disagree about speaker segments, timing, and words without throwing away either signal.
notes.wh: DOVER/ROVER-style systems typically combine one output type, while meeting hypotheses disagree in both diarization and ASR boundaries.
notes.naive: Vote words independently or concatenate the best diarization and best transcript as if their time intervals matched.
notes.ap: Use MOVER’s staged alignment, segment grouping, word/timing combination, and speaker reconciliation across complete meeting hypotheses.
notes.mech: The method constructs correspondences between speaker-labeled time intervals before combining words and timings, preserving the meeting structure.
notes.math: Combination is a structured matching problem over intervals, labels, and sequences rather than token-majority voting alone.
notes.eval: Combination is a structured matching problem over intervals, labels, and sequences rather than token-majority voting alone.
notes.ww: MOVER reports successful combination on CHiME-8 DASR and NOTSOFAR-1 multi-channel tasks.
notes.limits: Task formats, diarization errors, interval alignment, system diversity, and scoring rules bound transfer; fusion gains do not prove every component is complementary.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: NeuroSpex+: Dual-Task Training of Neuro-Guided Speaker Extraction with Speech Envelope and Waveform
notes.bp: A listener’s attended speaker should be isolated from a multi-talker scene using neural activity as a reference cue.
notes.wh: EEG-derived cues are noisy and indirect, and a separator that reconstructs a waveform may ignore the speech envelope that carries attention information.
notes.naive: Train only for waveform reconstruction or use an acoustic speaker cue when the target is defined neurally.
notes.ap: Train jointly to reconstruct both target waveform and target speech envelope, reinforcing the extraction mask.
notes.mech: A shared model predicts the target signal and its envelope; the dual losses constrain both fine waveform detail and slower attended-speech structure.
notes.math: Multi-task objectives shape the latent mask toward a target defined by two related projections of the attended speaker.
notes.eval: Multi-task objectives shape the latent mask toward a target defined by two related projections of the attended speaker.
notes.ww: NeuroSpex+ reports improved overall signal quality over baselines in the evaluated neuro-guided extraction setting.
notes.limits: EEG alignment, subjects, mixtures, signal metric, and lab conditions bound transfer; signal quality is not a demonstrated BCI communication benefit.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Breaking Resource Barriers in Speech Emotion Recognition via Data Distillation
notes.bp: An emotion recognizer should fit an IoT device without retaining a large private emotional-speech dataset.
notes.wh: Memory and compute constrain edge models, while emotional speech can carry sensitive information that should not be distributed unnecessarily.
notes.naive: Compress the model alone or train on a random small subset and assume it preserves the full-data decision boundary.
notes.ap: Distill a smaller synthetic dataset that retains training utility under fixed initialization, then train resource-constrained SER models on it.
notes.mech: The distilled set approximates the information needed by the learner; performance on held-out emotion recognition tests measures retained utility.
notes.math: Data distillation shifts compression from parameters to examples, trading dataset fidelity and privacy exposure against model performance.
notes.eval: Data distillation shifts compression from parameters to examples, trading dataset fidelity and privacy exposure against model performance.
notes.ww: The paper reports comparable SER performance between models trained on distilled and original emotional-speech data.
notes.limits: Synthesis method, emotion labels, initialization, privacy threat model, device profile, and test split bound the result; utility parity is not formal privacy.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: DiffDSR: Dysarthric Speech Reconstruction Using Latent Diffusion Model
notes.bp: Reconstruct dysarthric speech so it becomes more intelligible while retaining the original speaker identity.
notes.wh: Dysarthria damages content cues and voice characteristics together; improving intelligibility can erase identity or hallucinate phonemes.
notes.naive: Enhance the waveform generically or optimize intelligibility while ignoring speaker identity.
notes.ap: Restore phoneme embeddings with a pretrained speech encoder, preserve speaker information through an identity encoder, and generate speech with latent diffusion.
notes.mech: Separate content and identity conditioning feed a diffusion generator that samples a reconstructed waveform in latent space.
notes.math: The system imposes two invariants on generation: linguistic content must be restored while speaker identity remains in the conditioning path.
notes.eval: The system imposes two invariants on generation: linguistic content must be restored while speaker identity remains in the conditioning path.
notes.ww: The paper reports improved intelligibility and speaker similarity in its dysarthric speech reconstruction evaluation.
notes.limits: Speaker, severity, reference data, perceptual metrics, and diffusion sampling bound transfer; reconstructed speech is not clinical treatment evidence.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Tonal Variation and Word Meaning in Taiwanese
notes.bp: Tone realization in Taiwanese should be interpreted with word meaning and sandhi context rather than reduced to citation-tone substitution.
notes.wh: Tone sandhi changes non-final syllables and spontaneous speech varies; a raw sandhi-versus-citation comparison can mistake lexical meaning for phonological neutralization.
notes.naive: Assign one canonical tone to each lexical item or compare citation and sandhi forms without semantic context.
notes.ap: Analyze spontaneous high-falling tone realizations while modeling word meaning and compare residual sandhi/citation differences.
notes.mech: Acoustic tone measurements are grouped by lexical/semantic context, allowing meaning-induced variation to be separated from categorical tone effects.
notes.math: The analysis treats linguistic meaning as a conditioning variable in the acoustic realization, not as nuisance variance to average away.
notes.eval: The analysis treats linguistic meaning as a conditioning variable in the acoustic realization, not as nuisance variance to average away.
notes.ww: Word meaning explains part of tonal variability; after accounting for it, the reported sandhi/citation difference disappears.
notes.limits: Speaker sample, spontaneous corpus, lexical items, tone context, and statistical model bound transfer; one tone pattern is not the whole Taiwanese system.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.
